findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "check_mcp_capability" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "check_mcp_capability" references sensitive artifacts (bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "check_mcp_capability" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_mcp_capability · Private data: check_mcp_capability · Public sink: check_mcp_capability.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_mcp_capability · Private data: check_mcp_capability · Public sink: check_mcp_capability

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
